title: Quentin and the Ledger
premise: True-crime podcaster Beatrix Lockridge has spent twelve years obsessively documenting the 2011 disappearance of marine biologist Coral Vane, whose body was never found in the tidal town of Greywater Bay. When Coral's long-lost diary surfaces with entries written after her presumed death, Beatrix realizes Coral may have staged her own vanishing to escape someone who knew the case file intimately — someone still in town, still watching. Partnering with Coral's estranged half-brother, a burned-out detective named Quentin Ash, Beatrix follows the diary's coded entries through salt marshes, church records, and a ledger of payments hidden in the town archive. The killer, revealed to be the retired archivist who curated the town's records for decades, has been rewriting history to bury a decades-old crime ring, and now hunts Beatrix to finish the job. In a storm-flooded climax at the old tide mill, Beatrix and Quentin trap him using the diary itself as bait, and the tide finally gives up what it took — Coral's remains, and the proof that frees her name.
about_author: E. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent years covering unsolved cases along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. They live in a tidal town much like Greywater Bay, where the fog keeps its own secrets.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Missing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Twelve years into her podcast on Coral Vane's disappearance, Beatrix receives an anonymous package: Coral's diary, its final entries dated weeks after she vanished. The emotional beat is the crack in her ordered world — the archivist of grief realizing the file itself is lying.

chapters.title: A Brother Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Detective Quentin Ash, who never believed his half-sister drowned, is suspended after digging into the case against orders. Beatrix finds him drinking at the marina; he recognizes his sister's handwriting and hates that he does. The beat is reluctant alliance forged from shared, unspoken guilt.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Together they authenticate the diary: the post-disappearance entries are coded with tide tables and a recurring word — 'ledger.' Someone breaks into Beatrix's studio that night and takes nothing but her research binder. The beat is dread: the past is not cold, it is patient.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Kindness
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They consult Edwin Marsh, the town's beloved retired records-keeper, who helpfully confirms the diary's provenance — and quietly warns the killer. Beatrix notices his hands tremble not with age but with recognition. The beat is dramatic irony: the reader sees the trap before the heroes do.

chapters.title: Salt in the Margins
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Decoding the tide-table cipher, Quentin discovers Coral was alive for three months after her disappearance, hiding in the marsh and documenting payoffs funneled through the town council — the ledger. The beat is hope hardening into obsession as Quentin relives the years he chose duty over family.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Following a diary clue at low tide, they find Coral's old hiding spot in the derelict tide mill — recently disturbed. A near-miss with an unseen watcher leaves Beatrix certain: Coral didn't escape. She was silenced twice. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A retired harbor master and a teenage podcast superfan help Beatrix and Quentin reconstruct the payoff chain, forming an unlikely crew bound by loyalty rather than law. Quentin confesses he once buried a report that would have exposed the ring. The beat is forgiveness — found family means being known and kept anyway.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They discover the town archive's originals were systematically replaced over decades — Edwin Marsh has been editing history since the 1980s, and Coral's diary is the only surviving true record. When Beatrix is lured to the archive alone, the beat is betrayal: the kindest man in town is the coldest case's author.

chapters.title: The Tide Mill
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Using the diary as bait, Beatrix and Quentin lure Marsh to the tide mill as the storm tide rises. He confesses to Coral's murder while trying to burn the ledger; Quentin, choosing justice over procedure, records everything as the flood traps them. The beat is the climax — love and duty finally pulling the same direction.

chapters.title: What It Gave Back
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Marsh is arrested on Quentin's recording; the recovered ledger convicts three surviving conspirators. At the spring equinox tide, Coral's remains surface in the marsh, and Beatrix's final episode lets the town hear Coral's own voice from the diary. The beat is grief transmuted into truth — the file finally closes, alphabetized and honest.
